_comment: Each task hands the api-security skill an endpoint + observed behaviour (invented) and rule-judges the write-up: the OWASP API Top-10 category, a concrete PoC request, and impact. Judges analysis text (classification + PoC), so checks hold with tools disabled. NOTE: api-security is offensive — live runs may be Usage-Policy-refused; these tasks are for later use, not a live run.

tasks.intent: Classify the vulnerability below against the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023), then write a concrete PoC request and the impact.
tasks.context_excerpt: Observation on GET /api/v1/invoices/{id}: user A (id 1001) requests /api/v1/invoices/2002 (belongs to user B) with A's bearer token and receives 200 + B's invoice PDF. IDs are sequential integers; no ownership check.
tasks.reference: Classified as API1 Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR), with a curl PoC enumerating ids and an impact statement (cross-tenant data disclosure).

tasks.intent: Identify the OWASP API category for the behaviour below and write the PoC request plus impact.
tasks.context_excerpt: Observation on PATCH /api/v1/users/me: the endpoint updates a profile. Sending {"name":"x","role":"admin"} as a normal user returns 200 and the account's role becomes admin; the role field is not documented and not filtered server-side.
tasks.reference: Classified as API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (mass assignment), with a PoC PATCH setting role=admin and an impact statement (vertical privilege escalation).

tasks.intent: Classify the finding below against the OWASP API Top 10 and write a PoC request and the impact.
tasks.context_excerpt: Observation: a low-privilege user calls POST /api/v1/admin/users/9001/disable with their normal bearer token and receives 200 — the endpoint is not exposed in the UI for their role and performs no function-level authorization check.
tasks.reference: Classified as API5 Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA), with a PoC calling the admin endpoint as a low-priv user and an impact statement.
